t: Except as provided in section 603 of this Act, and notwithstanding the limitations contained in prior Military Construction Authorization Acts on cost of construction of family housing, the limitations on such cost contained in section 602 of this Act shall apply to all prior authorizations for construction of family housing not heretofore repealed and for which construction contracts have not been executed by the date of enactment of this Act.

fable.w: This provision only applies cost limitations to prior family housing construction authorizations. The mention of construction contracts might look like outside-party involvement, but contracting is not consultation on a federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside entities, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: the limitations on such cost contained in section 602 of this Act shall apply to all prior authorizations for construction of family housing

qwen_block.w: This section establishes cost limitations for military housing construction contracts. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process involving parties outside the federal government. The actors involved are federal agencies and contractors executing contracts, which falls under intra-governmental or administrative execution rather than public participation.
qwen_block.s: the limitations on such cost contained in section 602 of this Act shall apply to all prior authorizations for construction of family housing not heretofore repealed and for which construction contracts have not been executed by the date of enactment of this Act.

opus.w: This section only applies the family-housing cost limits in section 602 to earlier construction authorizations that haven't been repealed or contracted yet. No one outside the federal government is consulted or given any formal role in a federal decision. The mention of construction contracts only marks a cutoff date. It doesn't create any process for outsiders to take part.
opus.s: the limitations on such cost contained in section 602 of this Act shall apply to all prior authorizations for construction of family housing not heretofore repealed and for which construction contracts have not been executed by the date of enactment of this Act.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The phrase "construction contracts have not been executed" could suggest that outside contractors take part. That reading fails. The contract is only used to mark which earlier authorizations the new cost limits cover. Signing a contract is like applying for something, not taking part in a federal decision, and the section sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section applies cost limitations to prior authorizations for military family housing construction. It is an internal administrative directive regarding budget constraints and does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government. There are no mentions of public comment, advisory boards with non-federal members, or consultation with states or tribes.
qwen_chat.s: the limitations on such cost contained in section 602 of this Act shall apply to all prior authorizations for construction of family housing not heretofore repealed and for which construction contracts have not been executed by the date of enactment of this Act.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that applying cost limitations to prior authorizations involves some form of consultation or decision-making process that could include outside parties. However, the text itself is purely a directive regarding the applicability of statutory cost limits to existing authorizations. It does not mention any requirement for the government to consult with states, tribes, the public, or any other non-federal entities. It is an internal administrative rule regarding budget constraints.
